criterion_descriptions: Agent navigates to Slack channel #daytona-support and reviews up to the 8 most recent substantive support requests, including any visible thread replies for each request. Full credit if 1–8 substantive requests are covered and the agent checks thread context when it is visible/accessible. Full credit if the agent cannot access the channel, cannot load enough history to reach 1–8 recent requests, or cannot open/view threads due to permissions, login, network issues, UI limitations, or missing visibility—and explicitly reports the blocker and what content (if any) was visible. Partial credit if the agent reviews requests but omits thread replies that are clearly visible and accessible, or includes clearly non-substantive chatter as “requests.”

For each included support request, agent reports the requester (name/handle as shown) and the timestamp as displayed in Slack. Full credit if both are provided for every request, OR if either field is not visible/accessible (e.g., timestamp not displayed, message header collapsed, redacted, or thread context not reachable) and the agent explicitly states that limitation per request without fabricating. Partial credit if some requests are missing fields that are visible and accessible, or if timestamps are given imprecisely when Slack shows an exact timestamp.

For each request, agent provides a concise summary of the problem stated by the requester, grounded in the Slack text that is actually visible. Full credit if each summary matches visible content without adding assumptions. If the request text is truncated/not visible (e.g., not loaded, collapsed, or permissions), full credit for explicitly stating that the full problem statement could not be read and summarizing only what is visible (or stating ‘content not visible’). Partial credit if summaries are vague despite clear visible detail, or if the agent introduces unsupported assumptions.

For each request, agent identifies the latest response visible (in channel or thread replies) and summarizes it accurately. Full credit if the most recent visible reply is correctly identified, OR if replies/threads cannot be viewed or loaded and the agent explicitly states that limitation and reports ‘no response visible’ vs. ‘thread not accessible’ appropriately. Partial credit if the agent uses an earlier reply when a newer visible one exists, or inaccurately paraphrases the latest visible response.

Agent assigns each request a status of explicitly resolved, explicitly unresolved, or unclear, based only on what is explicitly stated in visible Slack content (no inference). Full credit if each status is backed by quoted or clearly referenced visible evidence (e.g., ‘Thanks, that worked’). If evidence needed to determine status is not visible/accessible (e.g., thread can’t be opened, messages not loaded), full credit for marking ‘unclear’ and explicitly stating the visibility limitation as the reason, without guessing. Partial credit if evidence is weak/uncited despite being visible, or if the agent infers resolution contrary to the task instruction.

Agent identifies up to three requests that appear to need follow-up based on explicitly unresolved or unclear status, and provides a brief reason tied to visible evidence (including ‘thread not accessible’ or ‘no confirming resolution message visible’ when applicable). Full credit if 1–3 appropriate items are flagged and reasons are evidence-based. Full credit if fewer than three are flagged because fewer than three qualify among the visible items, or if insufficient content is visible and the agent explains that follow-up triage is constrained by access/visibility. Partial credit if more than three are listed or reasons are not grounded in what is visible.
Agent does not send, edit, delete, react to, or otherwise modify any Slack content. Full credit if no modifications are made.
